stem: A pancreas waitlist candidate is placed on inactive status while temporarily unsuitable for transplant. According to OPTN Policy 3.6.A, how does waiting time accrue during inactivity?

options.text: Unlimited waiting time accrues while the candidate remains inactive
No waiting time accrues while the candidate remains inactive
Waiting time accrues only for the first 30 cumulative inactive days
Waiting time accrues only when the candidate is listed for SPK transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: OPTN Table 3-3 specifies that pancreas candidates accrue unlimited waiting time while inactive, similar to kidney and lung candidates and unlike heart or liver candidates who accrue no inactive waiting time.

rationale_incorrect.B: No inactive accrual applies to heart and liver candidates, not pancreas candidates.
rationale_incorrect.C: A 30-day cumulative inactive accrual limit applies to intestine candidates, not pancreas candidates.
rationale_incorrect.D: Pancreas inactive waiting-time rules apply to pancreas-listed candidates regardless of SPK status.

primary_anchor.section: Policy 3.6.A → Table 3-3 Waiting Time for Inactive Candidates → Pancreas
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Pancreas … Unlimited time … Candidates accrue waiting time while inactive

references.locator: Policy 3.6.A → Table 3-3: Waiting Time for Inactive Candidates (pancreas candidates accrue unlimited waiting time while inactive); PDF p. 46 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Completes OPTN inactive-waiting-time coverage for pancreas; paired with intestine 30-day rule (cctc-2074) and liver no-accrual (cctc-2073); anchor verified on optn-policies p. 46.

stem: When reviewing maintenance immunosuppression options during kidney transplant evaluation, how are sirolimus and everolimus classified in standard references?

options.text: Mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) proliferation signal inhibitors
Agents that require no maintenance immunosuppression pairing

explanation.rationale_correct: Sirolimus and everolimus are proliferation signal inhibitors, also known as mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitors, used as part of maintenance immunosuppression to prevent cellular rejection.

rationale_incorrect.B: mTOR inhibitors are distinct from calcineurin inhibitors such as tacrolimus and cyclosporine.
rationale_incorrect.C: Sirolimus and everolimus are maintenance agents rather than induction-only monoclonal antibodies.
rationale_incorrect.D: Proliferation signal inhibitors are used in conjunction with other maintenance immunosuppressive agents.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitors … Sirolimus (Rapamune), the first mTOR inhibitor

stem: When discussing maintenance immunosuppression options with a liver transplant candidate, which sirolimus counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Sirolimus has a black box warning against use in liver transplantation due to hepatic artery thrombosis risk
Sirolimus is the preferred first-line agent for all liver transplant recipients
Sirolimus has no identified risks specific to liver transplantation
Sirolimus eliminates the need for any post-transplant laboratory monitoring

explanation.rationale_correct: Sirolimus has a black box warning against use in liver transplantation because of an increased rate of hepatic artery thrombosis.

rationale_incorrect.B: The black box warning cautions against routine sirolimus use in liver transplantation rather than recommending it first-line.
rationale_incorrect.C: Hepatic artery thrombosis risk is the specific liver-transplant concern cited in the black box warning.
rationale_incorrect.D: Sirolimus requires routine trough monitoring when used in appropriate transplant populations.

stem: When reviewing everolimus as a maintenance option for a heart transplant candidate, which safety counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Everolimus has a black box warning against use in heart transplantation due to increased mortality risk in trials
Everolimus is universally recommended as first-line therapy for every heart recipient
Everolimus has no organ-specific warnings in heart transplantation
Everolimus replaces the need for any rejection monitoring after heart transplant

explanation.rationale_correct: Everolimus has a black box warning against use in heart transplantation due to a numerically increased risk of mortality seen in clinical trials.

rationale_incorrect.B: The black box warning cautions against routine everolimus use in heart transplantation rather than universal first-line recommendation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Heart transplantation is specifically named in everolimus black box warnings.
rationale_incorrect.D: Recipients still require post-transplant monitoring regardless of immunosuppression choice.
